```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
`%||%` <- function(x, y) if (is.null(x)) y else x
```

Every table the package returns is documented in a machine-readable
data dictionary shipped with the package, written in the
[data-dict.yaml](https://data-dict.tidyverse.org) format (spec 0.1.0):
column types, ranges, representative values, masking semantics,
cross-table relationships, and a glossary of TEA vocabulary. This
vignette *renders that file* -- it is generated from the same
dictionary your code can read, so the two can never drift apart:

```{r read}
dict <- yaml::read_yaml(
  system.file("data-dict.yaml", package = "txschools")
)
length(dict$tables)
```

Two conventions apply everywhere and are worth internalizing before
reading the tables:

* **Years are ending years.** `year = 2025` means the 2024-25 school
  year, matching TEA's URLs; `school_year` is the label form.
* **Identifiers are zero-padded strings.** Campus numbers are nine
  digits, district numbers six; keeping them as strings preserves
  leading zeros.

```{r render, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
one_line <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) "" else gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(x))
}

fmt_type <- function(col) {
  ty <- col$type %||% ""
  if (!is.null(col$units)) ty <- paste0(ty, " [", col$units, "]")
  ty
}

fmt_vals <- function(col) {
  if (!is.null(col$values)) {
    v <- col$values
    if (is.list(v) && !is.null(names(v))) {
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", names(v)), collapse = ", ")
    } else {
      paste(sprintf("`%s`", unlist(v)), collapse = ", ")
    }
  } else if (!is.null(col$range)) {
    paste0(col$range[[1]], " to ", col$range[[2]])
  } else if (!is.null(col$examples)) {
    paste(sprintf("`%s`", unlist(col$examples)), collapse = ", ")
  } else {
    ""
  }
}

fmt_req <- function(col) {
  cns <- unlist(col$constraints)
  if (is.null(cns)) return("")
  if ("primary_key" %in% cns) "key" else if ("required" %in% cns) "yes" else ""
}

for (tb in dict$tables) {
  cat("\n## ", tb$label %||% tb$name, "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("**`", tb$name, "`** — ", one_line(tb$description), "\n\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(tb$details)) cat(one_line(tb$details), "\n\n", sep = "")
  cols <- data.frame(
    column = vapply(tb$columns, function(cl) paste0("`", cl$name, "`"), ""),
    type = vapply(tb$columns, fmt_type, ""),
    required = vapply(tb$columns, fmt_req, ""),
    description = vapply(tb$columns, function(cl) one_line(cl$description), ""),
    `values / examples` = vapply(tb$columns, fmt_vals, ""),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  print(knitr::kable(cols, row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n")
}
```

# How the tables relate

```{r relationships, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
rel <- data.frame(
  join = vapply(dict$relationships, function(r) paste0("`", r$join, "`"), ""),
  cardinality = vapply(dict$relationships, function(r) r$cardinality %||% "", ""),
  description = vapply(dict$relationships, function(r) one_line(r$description), ""),
  check.names = FALSE
)
print(knitr::kable(rel, row.names = FALSE))
```

# Glossary

```{r glossary, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
for (term in names(dict$glossary)) {
  cat("**", term, "** — ", one_line(dict$glossary[[term]]), "\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

# Using the dictionary programmatically

The dictionary is plain YAML, so anything -- your code, a colleague's
Python, an AI agent -- can consume it directly:

```{r programmatic, eval = FALSE}
dict <- yaml::read_yaml(system.file("data-dict.yaml", package = "txschools"))

# Column names of the PEIMS finance table:
peims <- Filter(function(t) t$name == "peims_finance", dict$tables)[[1]]
vapply(peims$columns, `[[`, "", "name")
```

The [data-dict CLI](https://data-dict.tidyverse.org) can validate the
file against the specification, and the same conventions (one
`data-dict.yaml` per data collection) work for documenting your own
derived datasets downstream.
